content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Payments has 7 sick absences logged between 06:33 and 08:25, against a usual 2 per day. All notes say flu. Agents on phones are 13 against 18 planned (-28%) and were short from 08:00. Volume is only slightly above forecast (+5.4%) with no dominant reason, and AHT is near forecast. There are no incidents or marketing entries. This is a supply shortfall from sickness, not a demand surge, and SL fell to 58.1% at 08:45. General is broadly on forecast and staffed to plan (84.6% SL).","plan_name":"Payments sick-wave cover: overtime backfill plus short-term buffers","rationale":"The roughly 5-agent hole on payments is likely to last all day, so the main lever is consecutive 2-hour overtime offers on payments. Each offer goes to 8 agents; about 40% accept, giving about 3 extra agents. Five blocks from 09:30 to 19:30 cost about Rs 11,520, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Until overtime agents arrive at 09:30, the morning is bridged three ways. First, 2 cross-skilled agents move from general to payments, which is small enough to keep general above 70%. Second, payments breaks are delayed and coaching is cancelled for the morning. Third, a modest chat deflection takes status enquiries. A callback offer on payments for the rest of the day handles residual peaks with mild customer impact. No outage message is used because no outage is
